author: Traditionally Luke, a doctor and companion of Paul
authorNote: The Gospels do not name their authors; the names come from early church tradition, which scholars weigh differently.
audience: Theophilus and a wider non-Jewish audience
overview: Luke writes "an orderly account" of Jesus' life, from his birth in Bethlehem to his ascension. It highlights Jesus' care for the poor, women, outsiders and sinners, with parables like the Good Samaritan and the Prodigal Son. Luke continues the story in Acts.
storyPlace: Part one of a two-volume work (Luke–Acts).
